title: Marvel Has Assigned 42 Hours of Homework Before ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
gist: Marvel and Disney+ published an official 15-title, 42-hour 'Countdown to Doomsday' watchlist and companion podcast ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's December 18 theatrical release, a promotional move that doubles as a tactic to keep subscribers engaged with the streaming service.

insights.claim: Disney+ and Marvel released an official 15-title 'Countdown to Doomsday' watchlist plus a weekly recap podcast, requiring about 42 hours of viewing to complete before Avengers: Doomsday opens December 18.
insights.speaker: Megan Tomos
insights.so_what: Illustrates how studios use tentpole releases to manufacture recurring engagement on their owned streaming platform ahead of a theatrical event.
insights.quote: Marvel released an official “Countdown to Doomsday” playlist with Disney+, featuring 15 official selections to help fans catch up on all the action before watching the new movie.

insights.claim: A studio-issued pre-release watchlist functions as a subscriber-retention mechanism because it converts theatrical hype into recurring viewing on a service that must justify its monthly subscription cost.
insights.speaker: Megan Tomos
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern: franchise owners can use their back catalog to convert single-ticket theatrical demand into recurring subscription-service engagement.
insights.quote: Disney+ releasing a homework list for its own film is a great bit of subscriber farming.
insights.locator: The official movie watch list will require 42 hours

insights.claim: The 42-hour required watchlist works out to roughly under three hours per week if spread evenly over the roughly three months between the article's publication and the film's December 18 release.
insights.speaker: Megan Tomos
insights.so_what: Shows the pacing studios can design into engagement campaigns to sustain interest across a long pre-release window.
insights.locator: The official movie watch list will require 42 hours

insights.claim: Two X-Men films from 2000 and 2003 that predate the Marvel Cinematic Universe were included on the official Doomsday watchlist, which fans read as a signal that Patrick Stewart, James Marsden, Ian McKellen, and Alan Cumming are rumored to return for the new film.
insights.speaker: Megan Tomos
insights.so_what: Fan-facing marketing choices (which back-catalog titles get promoted) can serve as informal casting confirmation ahead of official studio announcements.
insights.locator: Devoted fans were quick to spot

insights.claim: The Marvels, a 2023 MCU film, was notably left off the official Doomsday watchlist despite being part of the franchise's recent output.
insights.speaker: Megan Tomos
insights.so_what: A curated omission from official marketing material can hint at which storylines or films a studio considers less central to its go-forward narrative.
insights.quote: The Marvels from 2023, interestingly, did not make the cut.
insights.locator: Devoted fans were quick to spot
